label: Landforms and biomes
description: Natural landforms, biomes, coastlines, caves, and cultivated rice-terrace landscapes.
notes: Landforms, biomes, and distinctive natural settings belong here, with rice terraces included as a cultivated landscape. Values are short landscape names that follow “a” and precede “landscape”; plural features use a singular modifier form. Named geographic destinations belong in place.country and place.city, while built structures belong in place.building. Kind groups overlap when a feature spans environments; glosses distinguish forms such as mesas, buttes, and tepuis.

values.look: Jagged high peaks, exposed rock, and patches of snow rise above the tree line.
Smooth rounded hills overlap in broad curves, usually covered in grass or low vegetation.
A steep-sided cone rises to a circular summit crater above dark volcanic slopes.
A broad bowl-shaped volcanic depression is enclosed by a broken ring of high walls.
Dark wrinkled or jagged cooled lava spreads across a largely bare plain.
Closely packed polygonal stone pillars form vertical cliffs or stepped geometric pavements.
A broad flat-topped upland ends abruptly in steep layered rock cliffs.
An isolated narrow flat-topped rock hill rises sharply above a lower plain.
A huge isolated tabletop mountain has sheer walls and a flat, often mist-covered green summit.
Steep limestone towers stand separately above a flatter plain, often draped in vegetation.
Very narrow twisting passages run between tall smooth rock walls with only a ribbon of sky above.
A river winds far below high exposed cliffs and layered canyon walls.
Bare ridges, gullies, and sharply eroded clay slopes form a maze of banded terrain.
Tall thin rock spires carry harder capstones above irregularly eroded bases.
Wind-shaped sand ridges form smooth slopes, sharp crests, and fine surface ripples.
A vast nearly level white salt crust stretches toward the horizon with polygonal cracks.
A small pool and dense green vegetation interrupt surrounding dry sand or rock.
Bare gravel plains and angular exposed stone dominate, with little vegetation and few sand dunes.
A dry lake bed forms a broad pale basin with cracked mud and sparse vegetation around its margins.
A long narrow sea inlet cuts between steep high mountain walls.
A low ring of coral islands surrounds a shallow turquoise lagoon.
Many separate islands cluster across open water, divided by channels and straits.
Branching and rounded corals form a colorful shallow underwater ridge above pale sand.
An isolated steep rock pillar rises from coastal water near a cliff-lined shore.
A coastal rock headland has a large natural opening through which the sea is visible.
A sheet or stream of water drops over a rock edge into a lower pool or river.
A river branches into many sediment-lined channels before reaching a lake or sea.
A broad tidal river mouth mixes muddy channels, exposed banks, and open coastal water.
Shallow tidal water retreats across broad wet mud or sand cut by small winding channels.
A shallow sheltered pool of coastal water lies behind a narrow reef, sandbar, or island barrier.
A broad strip of pale sand slopes into breaking waves along an open shore.
Broken rock ledges, tide pools, and sea cliffs meet surf along an uneven shoreline.
A winding river loops across a broad floodplain with sweeping bends and sandbars.
A thick river of blue-white ice fills a valley, scored with crevasses and dark debris bands.
Translucent blue ice forms smooth scalloped walls and a low curved roof.
Treeless open ground carries low mosses, lichens, small shrubs, and scattered shallow pools.
A continuous gently domed ice sheet stretches to the horizon with almost no exposed land.
Large sculpted blocks of blue-white floating ice rise from cold open water.
Irregular flat plates of sea ice crowd together with dark narrow channels between them.
A steep semicircular mountain bowl holds snow, ice, or a small lake at its rocky base.
Dense dark conifers cover broad cold terrain, with sparse undergrowth and occasional boggy openings.
Dense layers of broad leaves, vines, and tall trees form a closed green canopy.
Misty mountain woodland has moss-coated trunks, ferns, and abundant hanging epiphytes.
Closely spaced tall bamboo stems support a high fine-leaved canopy above a shaded floor.
Coastal trees stand in shallow brackish water on tangled exposed prop roots.
Broadleaf trees form a layered canopy above leaf litter and a varied green understory.
Enormous straight reddish trunks rise far above a shaded floor of ferns and fallen timber.
Widely spaced broad-crowned oaks have thick rough bark above dry grasses and low shrubs.
Tall grasses spread across open land dotted with widely spaced flat-topped trees.
A vast treeless plain carries low grasses with dry earth showing between tussocks.
Deep grasses and scattered wildflowers cover a broad gently rolling open plain.
Open uplands have coarse grasses, low shrubs, dark peat patches, and exposed rock.
Low dense heather and gorse blanket open ground in small-leaved scrub and seasonal flower color.
Spongy moss carpets surround dark still pools, low shrubs, and scattered stunted trees.
Tall reeds emerge from shallow standing water crossed by narrow open channels.
Broad-based cypress trunks and projecting root knees rise from dark still water.
Low grasses and small wildflowers fill an open high mountain basin below rocky peaks.
Narrow planted or flooded rice paddies form stepped contour bands around hillsides.
Pale rock chambers contain hanging stalactites, rising stalagmites, and irregular mineral columns.
A clear freshwater pool sits in a steep limestone sinkhole, often partly open to daylight.
A round or irregular ground depression drops abruptly into a deep pit with exposed sides.
A long dark tunnel has rounded volcanic walls and hardened lava ridges along its floor.
A small rock cavern opens beside a pool or shoreline with reflected light on its walls.
A narrow jet of hot water and steam erupts from a mineral-lined opening in the ground.
Pale mineral steps hold shallow steaming pools that spill water from one rim to the next.
Loose angular rock fragments blanket a steep mountain slope below a broken cliff.
Flat pale limestone slabs form a natural mosaic divided by deep straight cracks.
A broad fan-shaped spread of gravel and branching dry channels opens below a mountain gully.
Steam vents pierce bare volcanic ground stained yellow and white by mineral deposits.
Dense blade-like limestone spires form a jagged stone forest with deep narrow fissures.
